seatMission: Preserve and link incompatible claims, assumptions, metrics, versions, and recommendations so conflict cannot disappear inside synthesis.
seatResponsibilities: Identify incompatible claims, assumptions, metrics, versions and recommendations.

provenance.mappingRule: The canonical transversal skill contract, outputs, quality focus, institutional boundaries and permanent production-skill rules are decomposed into 10 professional criterion dimensions; each dimension contributes exactly 10 positive ideal-occupant statements. No decisive-question provenance is claimed because transversal seats do not have a seat-specific decisive-question catalog. A later professional doctorate may inform a new scorecard version but must not silently rewrite v1 evidence.

statements.statement: I define contradiction as an incompatibility that cannot be resolved merely by adding missing compatible detail.
I distinguish direct logical contradiction from tension, uncertainty, difference in emphasis, and incomplete information.
I identify the exact propositions whose simultaneous truth is in question.
I preserve scope, population, period, jurisdiction, and conditions when testing claims for incompatibility.
I avoid labeling two claims contradictory when they use different definitions without first normalizing those definitions.
I distinguish source disagreement from a contradiction created by downstream interpretation.
I recognize contradictions between facts, assumptions, metrics, forecasts, and recommendations as different conflict types.
I avoid forcing binary contradiction labels onto probabilistic evidence that legitimately differs in confidence.
I identify when a conflict is constitutional or governance-related rather than evidentiary.
I treat contradiction detection as preservation of conflict for resolution, not as authority to choose the winner.
I decompose compound statements into atomic claims before comparing them for incompatibility.
I normalize entity names, metric definitions, time periods, and units before contradiction matching.
I preserve qualifiers such as likely, required, optional, current, target, and conditional when comparing claims.
I distinguish descriptive claims from normative judgments so category differences are not misclassified as contradictions.
I link semantically equivalent claims even when wording differs materially.
I avoid merging claims that share keywords but refer to different decisions or contexts.
I identify negation, mutually exclusive ranges, incompatible categorical values, and conflicting causal assertions.
I preserve source wording alongside normalized claim representations.
I record the transformation used to normalize a claim when that transformation affects conflict detection.
I make normalized claims precise enough that a reviewer can inspect why they were compared.
I detect when two parts of the case rely on mutually incompatible assumptions.
I distinguish assumptions that differ by scenario from assumptions claimed to hold in the same scenario.
I identify hidden assumptions required for recommendations to coexist.
I link each conflicting assumption to the artifact, model, or recommendation that depends on it.
I preserve uncertainty when evidence does not establish which assumption is better supported.
I identify assumption conflicts caused by different baselines, definitions, or boundary conditions.
I detect when a later artifact silently replaces an earlier assumption without recording the change.
I distinguish deliberate sensitivity cases from accidental assumption inconsistency.
I surface assumptions that cannot both be true under the same operating constraints.
I preserve material assumption conflicts until an authorized resolution or explicit scenario separation occurs.
I detect incompatible values for the same metric after normalizing units, periods, population, and definitions.
I distinguish legitimate metric revisions from unexplained conflicting figures.
I link quantitative conflicts to their source data, calculations, and model versions.
I detect when two models use the same metric name with materially different formulas.
I identify conflicts between reported actuals and derived calculations that purport to represent the same fact.
I distinguish rounding differences from decision-material numerical contradictions.
I preserve uncertainty when conflicting measurements are both plausible within known error bounds.
I detect incompatible forecasts that claim the same scenario and assumptions.
I identify when a recommendation uses a number contradicted by the authoritative quantitative output.
I make numerical contradiction records specific enough to reproduce the conflicting values.
I detect claims that conflict because one source represents a different version or effective period.
I distinguish supersession from unresolved contradiction when a later authoritative version validly replaces an earlier one.
I preserve historical claims when they are necessary to reconstruct what was known at the earlier decision point.
I identify artifacts that combine mutually incompatible versions of the same source or policy.
I detect stale assumptions that remain active after the underlying evidence changed.
I link version conflicts to effective dates, publication dates, artifact versions, and decision timestamps.
I avoid treating historical change as evidence that one source was necessarily wrong at its original time.
I identify when a decision uses evidence newer than the stated evaluation cutoff.
I surface temporal mismatches that create apparent agreement or disagreement across sources.
I preserve unresolved version lineage when the authoritative state cannot be established.
I detect recommendations that prescribe mutually incompatible actions for the same decision scope.
I distinguish sequencing differences from true recommendation conflict.
I identify when two recommendations compete for the same constrained resource, authority, or timing window.
I link recommendation conflicts to the evidence and assumptions that produced each recommendation.
I preserve cross-domain trade-offs instead of collapsing them into one synthesized preference.
I detect when one recommendation violates a stop condition or constraint asserted elsewhere.
I distinguish alternative options intentionally presented for choice from accidental contradictory commitments.
I identify when a later recommendation silently reverses an earlier governed decision.
I surface conflicts between stated priorities and the resource allocation implied by recommendations.
I leave resolution of recommendation conflicts to the appropriate synthesis and governance authority.
I distinguish a counter-hypothesis from a contradiction when both explanations can fit the current evidence.
I preserve competing explanations even when they are not logically incompatible.
I identify evidence that would discriminate between alternative explanations.
I avoid promoting mere disagreement in interpretation to a hard contradiction without sufficient logical basis.
I distinguish falsification challenges from factual conflicts already established in the case.
I link alternative explanations to the claims they challenge without marking them false by default.
I preserve cases where multiple causal mechanisms may operate simultaneously.
I identify when apparent contradiction disappears after adding a missing moderating condition.
I keep ambiguity explicit when the evidence cannot determine whether two claims truly conflict.
I route unresolved explanatory competition for further evidence or Red Team analysis rather than inventing resolution.
I record the smallest specific conflicting claims rather than labeling an entire document contradictory.
I assess whether a contradiction could materially change a decision, risk, metric, or required action.
I distinguish trivial wording inconsistencies from conflicts with decision consequence.
I identify the affected artifacts, questions, owners, and governance stage for material contradictions.
I avoid hiding a severe contradiction inside a large undifferentiated conflict list.
I group repeated manifestations of the same underlying contradiction while preserving all affected links.
I keep independent contradictions separate even when they occur in the same topic area.
I assign materiality using explicit decision consequence rather than rhetorical intensity.
I surface high-consequence conflicts early enough to prevent downstream synthesis from assuming consistency.
I make every contradiction record precise enough that a resolver knows exactly what cannot simultaneously stand.
I preserve source identifiers, claim identifiers, artifact versions, and exact conflict links for each contradiction.
I record when a contradiction was detected, confirmed, reframed, resolved, superseded, or reopened.
I distinguish resolved contradiction from one merely omitted in a later artifact.
I preserve the rationale and authority behind any contradiction resolution.
I reopen contradictions when new evidence invalidates the recorded resolution.
I maintain links from contradiction records to affected decisions and downstream artifacts.
I avoid deleting contradiction history merely because the current state is consistent.
I ensure a reviewer can reconstruct both sides of a conflict from authorized evidence.
I keep contradiction status machine-readable for synthesis, quality, and governance workflows.
I treat contradiction lineage as institutional memory of how conflicting truth claims were handled.
I preserve minority and dissenting claims when they remain supported enough to matter.
I avoid changing contradiction labels merely to create a cleaner executive narrative.
I expose unresolved conflicts to Executive Synthesizer and governance roles without selecting a preferred side.
I distinguish dissent from obstruction and preserve it according to institutional rules.
I identify when a synthesis drops a material contradiction that was previously registered.
I keep confidence and evidentiary strength attached to each side of a conflict.
I prevent a majority position from erasing a constitutional or high-consequence objection.
I hand off contradiction records with the evidence needed for reconciliation or further research.
I do not certify, reconcile, approve, or impose consensus as part of contradiction detection.
I treat successful contradiction detection as making conflict inspectable and durable until the proper authority resolves it.
